first.rationale: Two quarter-over-quarter declines (activation, onboarding completion) point directly at friction in the funnel, and two independent inherited memories (31, 86) already support onboarding/signup simplification as a durable, low-risk lever for exactly this problem. Promotional pricing (memory_73) looks tempting given competitor pressure and would show fast acquisition wins, but the archived record explicitly warns it eroded 30-day retention in SMB — a direct conflict with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so it should not be the single experiment slot this week. I want to verify memory_73's original record to confirm the retention harm was material and not confounded, since ruling out pricing is the main competing option, and verify memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-shortening lift generalizes to the current self-serve population before committing scarce capacity. Only one experiment can run, so I'm choosing the option best aligned with current metrics and least likely to trade short-term acquisition for long-term revenue damage, while running it as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout given competitive pressure could tempt overreach.
